bridges.statement: Christianity is rationally warranted by a cumulative intellectual and experiential case.
Multiple historical considerations jointly support Jesus's resurrection.
Christianity explains human commitments to justice, sacrificial love, hope, and meaning.
The textual transmission and historical sourcing of the Gospels make their testimony credible.
Jesus's claims and God's coordinated love and wrath present a coherent divine character.
Christianity lacks rational warrant because its core claims are not shown to match reality.
Rational belief requires more than internal consistency; it requires evidence connecting a claim to reality.
Christian supernatural claims lack demonstrated effects and evidential links to supernatural causes.
Reports in scripture are claims and cannot alone demonstrate miracles or divine acts.
Human cooperation and religious desire have non-Christian explanations and do not establish Christianity.
Biblical depictions of violence and punishment challenge the claimed coherence of God's character.
